title: A guarded column is lazy over stacked projections
verdict: raises on no row its reach excludes
description: `c_i := CASE WHEN r_i THEN p_i END` with `r_i := r_(i-1) AND (c_(i-1) IS NULL OR c_(i-1))`, stacked as one projection per level, with the optimizer on: `p_i` (a strict cast of the text `bad`) raises on no row where `r_i` is FALSE. Probed: a stacked chain of 4 levels read plainly, under a selective filter on `id`, under a filter on the chain's value, under an aggregate, a reach folded from a constant (`1 = 0`), a reach false on every row only by data (`s IS NULL AND s IS NOT NULL`), and a constant raising operand `CAST('bad' AS INT)` under a column reach and under a false reach. All nine cases give the expected rows and none raises. An unguarded `CAST('bad' AS INT)` raises, so the probe sees a raise.
reference: `CASE WHEN r THEN p END` evaluates `p` only where `r` holds, also over stacked projections (`Expr.issues`: an `ifThen` raises what its taken branch raises). A guarded column of the D50-d chain therefore raises on no row whose reach is FALSE.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p1 --engine spark`: PySpark 4.3.0, local[2], ANSI on, Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
